title: Bounded acyclic flat models represent the proper coefficient map termwise
statement:
Let $r:W\to V$ be a proper morphism [def-weil-proper-morphism] of Noetherian schemes [def-pc-scheme], meaning schemes admitting finite affine covers by spectra of Noetherian rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and let $A\to B$ be a unital homomorphism of finite commutative rings. Work with sheaves of modules over the constant ring sheaves on the small etale sites and their ordinary unbounded derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Write $T_T=-\otimes^L_{A_T}B_T$ and $\lambda:T_Wr_A^*\xrightarrow{\sim}r_B^*T_V$ for the canonical tensor/pullback comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. Define $q_r:T_VRr_{*,A}\to Rr_{*,B}T_W$ as the adjoint transpose under $r_B^*\dashv Rr_{*,B}$ of $T_W(\varepsilon_A)\circ\lambda^{-1}$, where $\varepsilon_A:r_A^*Rr_{*,A}\to1$ is the counit [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact, def-weil-pbc-direct-image].

Let $C$ be a cochain complex of $A_W$-module sheaves, zero outside a finite interval, and put $C_B=C\otimes_{A_W}B_W$ termwise. Assume each $C^n$ is flat over $A_W$, meaning tensoring with it is exact; assume each $r_{*,A}C^n$ is flat over $A_V$; and assume for every $n$ and every $a>0$ that
$$R^ar_{*,A}(C^n)=0,\qquad R^ar_{*,B}(C^n\otimes_{A_W}B_W)=0.$$
Then the canonical acyclic-complex comparison maps identify $Rr_{*,A}C$ and $Rr_{*,B}C_B$ with the degreewise complexes $r_{*,A}C$ and $r_{*,B}C_B$, respectively. The complexes $C$ and $r_{*,A}C$ are K-flat (tensoring them with any acyclic complex gives an acyclic total tensor complex). Under these specified identifications and the flat-model identifications for $T$, the named map $q_r(C)$ is represented by the termwise sheaf projection morphism
$$\pi_C:(r_{*,A}C)\otimes_{A_V}B_V\longrightarrow r_{*,B}(C\otimes_{A_W}B_W),$$
whose degree-$n$ morphism is adjoint to
$$r_B^*((r_{*,A}C^n)\otimes_{A_V}B_V)\cong(r_A^*r_{*,A}C^n)\otimes_{A_W}B_W
\xrightarrow{\varepsilon_{A,C^n}\otimes1}C^n\otimes_{A_W}B_W.$$
The identifications and this representation are natural in chain maps between complexes satisfying these hypotheses. No flatness or finite projective dimension of $B$ over $A$ is assumed.

proof.text: Put D = r_* C and E = C_B. Additive functors preserve zero objects, so D has the same finite support bound as C and E retains its lower bound. Convert exactness of tensorRight with each term of C and D to exactness on both sides using braided symmetry. Apply the already proved source theorem CochainComplex.kFlat_of_bounded_of_flat to obtain the project's quasi-isomorphism K-flat predicates for C and D. This uses the existing ModuleCat-valued sheaf instances directly, without changing to the separate SheafOfModules encoding.

Identify positive homology of the unbounded right derived direct image of a single object with its classical positive right derived functors, using homologyRightDerivedFunctorObjSingleFunctorIso. Thus the terms of C and E are right acyclic. Apply the existing bounded-below acyclic-unit theorem [src-right-derived-functor-plus-acyclic-unit]. The canonical rightDerivedFunctorPlusCompatibility identifies its image under the bounded-below inclusion with rightDerivedFunctorUnit. Whiskering that unit with the homotopy quotient factor gives exactly properAcyclicComparison. Both canonical comparison maps are therefore invertible.

Reuse the proved preservation and derived-unit normalization results of [def-weil-pbc-witness-compatibility]. Let E_T be ordinary sheafified extension of scalars and U_T exact faithful restriction. The ordinary extension/restriction composite is tensorRight with the sheafification of the constant A-module B: compose sheafification/restriction compatibility, ModuleCat.extendScalarsCompRestrictScalarsIso and the sheafification/tensor comparison. Acyclic tensoring by a K-flat complex and faithfulness and exactness of U_T show that E_T preserves quasi-isomorphisms between K-flat complexes. Its left derived counit is consequently invertible on C and D. The chosen scalar-extension left adjoint is canonically isomorphic to this left derived functor by Adjunction.leftAdjointUniq. The derived-unit factorization and naturality of the exact restriction comparison identify scalarExtensionRepresentative with this isomorphism followed by the left derived counit. Hence both specified scalar representatives are invertible. This resolves the first tensor factor only and imposes no flatness condition on B.

proof.text: Use the unit and counit factorization equations of the canonical derived adjunctions, obtained from Adjunction.derivedη_fac_app and derivedε_fac_app with the homotopy quotient factors included. Apply the K-flat normalization of scalarPullbackIso from [def-pur-etale-scalar-pullback-iso] at D. A generic mate calculation expands both mates into unit, square and counit, moves the comparison maps by naturality, and substitutes those two factorization equations and the normalization at D. Its conclusion is the required displayed square. Mapping the ordinary mate to cochain complexes agrees degreewise with the mate of the mapped square; a generic additive-functor lemma verifies this by extensionality on each degree. Therefore the chain-map term in the square is exactly properCoefficientComplexMap, retaining the B-linear structure.

proof.text: Package the acyclic comparisons, the scalar representatives (transposes of the localized ordinary scalar unit), and the mapped ordinary coefficient mate as natural transformations. Their naturality gives the six required equations, with the mate equation in the stated orientation. These arguments apply to every chain map, hence in particular to maps between the stipulated bounded acyclic flat models.
